title: India cancels trains, deploys 23,000 police and shuts 45 Delhi metro stations to block CJP protest at Jantar Mantar
detail: Authorities cancelled trains to Delhi and flooded the capital with 23,000 police officers ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's planned protest at Jantar Mantar. Forty-five metro stations were shut as demonstrators began gathering. The sweeping security operation drew comparisons to tactics used against Kashmir protests.

media.caption: Security personnel deployed ahead of the CJP protest at New Delhi

title: Omar Abdullah condemns Delhi internet curbs ahead of CJP protest, compares capital's treatment to J&K under Article 370
detail: Jammu & Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah publicly condemned internet restrictions imposed across Delhi ahead of the CJP protest, stating that the national capital was being treated like Jammu & Kashmir was under Article 370. His remarks highlighted the escalating crackdown on the youth-led movement and drew national attention to civil liberties concerns.

media.caption: Omar Abdullah condemns internet curbs imposed in Delhi ahead of CJP protest

title: Kejriwal detained at Delhi protest, shares 'Youth has awakened' video message
detail: Arvind Kejriwal was detained during the Delhi anti-CEC protests and subsequently shared a video message declaring 'Youth has awakened', marking the first detention of a major national opposition leader in the government's crackdown on the Cockroach Janta Party movement.

media.caption: Arvind Kejriwal detained during Delhi protests, shares video message

title: Lawyers detained near Supreme Court during protest, released after Chief Justice intervention
detail: Lawyers demonstrating near the Supreme Court building were detained by Delhi police during the anti-CEC protest crackdown. They were released following direct intervention by the Chief Justice of India, exposing judiciary-executive tensions over the scope of the government's security response.

media.caption: Lawyers detained near India's Supreme Court during Delhi protest

title: Delhi police throw wide net of preventive detentions across capital ahead of anti-CEC protest
detail: Delhi police and security forces conducted large-scale preventive detentions across New Delhi ahead of and during the CJP's anti-Chief Election Commissioner protest, with demonstrators swept up across multiple locations throughout the capital in a sweeping security operation.

media.caption: Police preventive detentions sweep New Delhi during anti-CEC protest

title: CPI(M) leaders detained in Andhra Pradesh, 'Chalo Lok Bhavan' march foiled as crackdown spreads beyond Delhi
detail: Andhra Pradesh police took CPI(M) leaders into custody and prevented a planned 'Chalo Lok Bhavan' solidarity march, extending the government's crackdown on anti-CEC protest activity beyond Delhi to opposition-governed states, signalling a nationwide enforcement response.

media.caption: CPI(M) leaders detained in Andhra Pradesh as anti-CEC protest crackdown spreads

title: Journalists detained in Delhi's massive police crackdown on youth protest, raising press freedom concerns
detail: Members of the press were detained alongside protesters in Delhi's sweeping police crackdown on anti-CEC youth demonstrations, drawing condemnation from press freedom organisations and highlighting concerns about media access to protest coverage.

media.caption: Journalists detained during Delhi police crackdown on youth protest

title: New leader named for India's 'Cockroach' protest movement, signaling organizational continuity amid crackdown
detail: A new leader has been named for India's Cockroach Janta Party protest movement, signaling organizational continuity as the government continues its crackdown on the youth-led uprising. The naming of new leadership demonstrates the movement's resilience and decentralized structure, ensuring it can absorb arrests and detentions without losing momentum.

title: India's Supreme Court schedules emergency Sunday hearing on contempt plea over Delhi's October 10 transit shutdown
detail: India's Supreme Court has scheduled an emergency Sunday hearing on a contempt plea challenging Delhi's October 10 transit shutdown, which authorities used to suppress the anti-CEC youth protest. The scheduling of a weekend hearing underscores the legal urgency and judicial scrutiny of the government's sweeping crackdown measures.
